QuestInfo.name: We Hold Your Place
QuestInfo.0: #b#p402##k sent the ledger ahead to #b#p313##k in the #b#m010002003##k. The oldest part of the entry names him.
QuestInfo.1: #b#p313##k read the whole entry and couldn't make sense of it. He told me to take the ledger back up to #b#p326##k and ask her what it means.
QuestInfo.2: #b#p326##k explained what the entry really is, and she has written me into the registry.

0.0: Ah, it's you. You went up to the room above this one a while ago and came back down. I didn't pry at the time. \nThat route used to see a lot more traffic.
0.1: Hold that book up where I can see it. ...Ah. My name is right at the very top of this entry. \nI remember this traveler. They came to me wanting to be a magician, but they lacked the aptitude.
0.2: I told them 'no', right here in this room. A harsh refusal is the only thing that forces a novice to go out into the world, grow stronger, and prove me wrong. I do not regret it. \nHand the book here. I want to see what became of them after they walked out my door.
0.3: ...Wait. This makes no sense.\nIt says this same person went to #b#m010004000##k to become a warrior. But then it says they became a thief in #b#m010003000##k?
0.4: Then they dropped all their gear on a bench, started over, and here is my name again, telling them 'no' a second time. \nThis isn't one traveler living contradictory lives...
0.5: Those separate entries the others saw weren't chapters of one erratic life. Every line in this long record is a unique, personal moment lived by someone different. \nTheir paths might intersect in the same halls or at the same crossroads, but their choices and experiences were entirely their own. \n#b#p326##k let them share this entry so every individual story stands together.
0.6: Take it back to her. She didn't make a mistake—she chose to keep all those memories together, and she doesn't need an old scholar to explain her own book to her. Will you return it for me?

yes.0: Good.\nUp to the second level and over the shelves. She will not come down. Someone has to go up.

no.0: Then it stays down here with the rest of them, and nothing in this room has been opened in a very long time.

1.0: Oh, hey. You found them. Just put it on the desk. \n...Someone rebound it. And the ink is back. Every person you visited wrote their own notes in the margins. Stan, Manji, Alex... they each thought they were helping you track down the exact same traveler.
1.1: But Grendel saw what makes the main record so important, didn't he? \nThat long entry isn't one person doing impossible things, and it isn't a bunch of meaningless copies either. Every single entry in there was someone's real, personal moment.
1.2: They might pass through the same town, look for the same weapon, or get rejected by the same old man, but every journey belonged entirely to the person living it. I stopped separating them because all those individual memories deserve to stand side by side.\nAnd the receptionist in Sleepywood was right. There are zero closing lines in here.
1.3: I thought about writing them myself. It would be tidy, and the book would finally be finished.\nBut a closing line means somebody's journey is totally over. And I absolutely refuse to decide when someone is done.
1.4: So I just leave the rest of the page open.\nAnyway, the book is safe now. Thank you. You can go back to your adventure. I'll make sure your page stays open, too.
1.5: Oh, right. Take these gifts. I hope you always remember that your story is still being written!

npc.0: She is upstairs and she is not coming down. That much has been settled for some time.

item.0: You came all the way up here with nothing in your hands. That is all right. People do that too. Mostly by accident.

lost.0: You lost it. That is all right. I copy out everything I write, because things that only exist once tend not to. Here are the same words. Please do not make me find out whether I would write them a third time.
